action: Update PHP to 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13 and check for the non-default configurations the advisories describe.
exec: PHP's critical flaws need non-default or uncommon setups, but patching is advised.
plain: PHP released updates fixing 17 security flaws, several rated critical. Server owners should update.

key_findings: heise reports PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 and 8.5.13 fix 17 vulnerabilities, seven rated critical at CVSS 9.2.
heise describes code execution for some of them, each needing preconditions such as non-default settings (heise noted a miscount in its own tally).
The Register says CVE-2026-115560 is an RCE bug needing an unlikely mix of configuration and application code; no exploitation of this release is reported.
recommendations: Prepare to patch on release day.

summary: PHP shipped security releases 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 and 8.5.13, fixing 17 vulnerabilities, according to heise. heise reports seven rated critical (CVSS 9.2) and says some allow code execution, but only under preconditions and not on default installations. The Register says the critical issues need non-default configuration or uncommon setups.
title: PHP releases 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 and 8.5.13 fixing 17 vulnerabilities, several rated critical

validation.note: heise, The Register and SecurityWeek report independently; SecurityWeek lists seven critical RCE CVEs and links the php.net notice (php.net not opened); no exploitation of these seven is stated.

review.note: Checked versions, 17 vulnerabilities, seven critical CVSS 9.2, preconditions and non-default config wording, 19 Nov release against heise, The Register and SecurityWeek; no exploitation claimed
